## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components can approach the streaming ceiling on death-free workloads.

## Cache saturation
All tested N (10000–10000000) sit past the L2 spill at N≈7598; N=1000000 and N=10000000 also exceed the L3 spill at N≈243148. At death_q=0.01 the curve is essentially flat: 26.3 ns/p at N=10000, 25.6 at N=100000, 25.8 at N=1000000, and 26.6 at N=10000000. There is no knee at the L3→DRAM transition — cost stays within 1 ns/particle across a 1000× working-set range. Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the curve: the best ns/p climbs from 25.6 (q=0.01) to 26.4 (q=0.1), 28.1 (q=0.25), and 31.7 (q=0.5), all at N=100000. The absence of any cache-spill knee confirms the bottleneck is not data-movement capacity.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved bandwidth is 2.7 GB/s at N=100000, death_q=0.01 — only 21% of the 12.69 GB/s streaming ceiling. The algo is overhead-bound, not bandwidth-bound: perf attributes 68–84% of cycles to frontend_stall across every measured configuration, with compute at 27–36% (single-thread) and backend_stall near zero at q=0.01. There is no regime where bandwidth approaches the ceiling; even at the largest N and lowest death rate the algo stays at 2.5–2.7 GB/s. Raising death_q to 0.5 drops the floor to 2.0 GB/s, but the dominant cost remains frontend, not memory.

## Assembly
The compiler did not vectorize the per-particle computation. The histogram shows zero vector-suffixed instructions; all floating-point work is scalar — `vmovss` (8), `vmulss` (4), `vaddss` (1), `vsubss` (1), `vucomiss` (8), `vcvttss2si` (5). The only SIMD usage is a single `vmovdqu` + `vptest` pair that bulk-checks 32 spawn-flag bytes in the unrolled respawn loop. The scatter writes are byte-granular scalar stores (`mov BYTE PTR [rsi+r14*1], r13b` with `cmovae` clamping to 0xff), and 34 `vzeroupper` instructions precede 35 `call` sites into `spawn`. The 589-instruction body with 68 `cmp` and 43 `je` explains the 68%+ frontend stalls: the branchy, call-heavy control flow starves the fetch/decode pipeline, and the lack of vectorization explains why bandwidth stays at 21% of ceiling.

## Verdict
Refuted — the compiler emitted zero vector instructions (all scalar `vmovss`/`vmulss`), peak bandwidth reaches only 2.7 GB/s = 21% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling, and 68–84% frontend stalls confirm the algo is instruction-fetch-bound, not bandwidth-bound. Auto-vectorization did not occur and the streaming ceiling was never approached, regardless of death rate or N.
